title: Council rubric for one architecture redesign
scale: Real 0..1. Anchored at three points only; a member interpolates between them and says so in its confidence, it does not invent a fourth anchor.
notes: A redesign has no users of its own, so there is no value member and no rivalry member here. The value of a redesign is the value of the features that ride on it, and those are councilled as features.
The mechanical share is deliberately the majority: a redesign is judged mostly on properties that can be read off the diff and the migration, not on taste.
Reversibility is what makes a redesign safe to accept from an autonomous builder at all, which is why it carries a binding floor.

dimensions.weight_rationale: The largest share, because in a redesign the design IS the deliverable: there is no user-visible behaviour to compensate for a shape that will have to be undone.
dimensions.floor_rationale: No floor: a redesign that is merely adequate is still a decision for the person at the gate.
dimensions.question: Is the new shape the right one - against the standards this repo subscribes to and against current practice outside them?

levels.1.0: The new shape matches the governing golden path or names a deliberate, recorded deviation with its reason, and retires more hand-rolled copies than it adds abstractions.
levels.0.5: A defensible shape with at least one unrecorded departure from the standard, or a new abstraction with fewer than three call sites retired.
levels.0: The shape contradicts the standard that governs it with no recorded reason, or adds an abstraction nothing yet uses.

dimensions.weight_rationale: A redesign touches everything that already worked, so the largest mechanical share goes to the question of whether it still does.
dimensions.floor_rationale: Binding. A redesign whose own repo's gates do not pass over the span has already failed the only measurement available before it ships.
dimensions.question: Does the repo's own verification pass over the whole span, including every consumer the redesign moved?

levels.1.0: Every declared gate passes over the span, every consumer of the moved surface is enumerated by a command shown in the evidence, and each is covered.
levels.0.5: Gates pass but the consumer enumeration is asserted rather than shown, or one consumer is uncovered and named.
levels.0: A declared gate fails over this span, or a consumer of the moved surface was missed.

dimensions.weight_rationale: Weighted just below robustness because it is the property that converts a wrong redesign from a catastrophe into a bad week, and it is fully readable off the migration and the rollout.
dimensions.floor_rationale: Binding. An irreversible data rewrite accepted on an uncalibrated judged opinion is exactly the failure this whole method exists to prevent.
dimensions.question: If this redesign turns out to be wrong after it ships, what does undoing it cost?

levels.1.0: Every migration has a guard or a down path, the rollout lands per pull request behind a switch, and no step rewrites data irreversibly.
levels.0.5: Reversible with manual work: a down path exists but is untested, or the rollout is one landing that could be reverted as a whole.
levels.0: An irreversible data rewrite, a destructive migration with no down path, or a rollout that cannot be reverted once any consumer has read the new shape.

dimensions.weight_rationale: The smallest share for the same reason as in the feature rubric: it informs the trade the person makes at the gate and decides nothing by itself.
dimensions.floor_rationale: No floor: a redesign that costs more to run can still be the right shape.
dimensions.question: What does the new shape cost to run and to build against, compared with the old one?

levels.1.0: The change in running cost and in build time is measured against the old shape with named figures.
levels.0.5: The change is estimated from a named model rather than measured, and labelled as an estimate.
levels.0: The new shape adds an unbounded cost: an unbounded query, an uncapped fan-out, or a build step with no ceiling.

dimensions.not_applicable_when: the redesign is confined to a surface with no metered call and no measurable build or runtime cost difference
